text:
maria: Heads up — since ~06:02 UTC we're seeing a fleet-wide uptick in Xid and ECC errors impacting multiple zones. Capacity visible to autoscaler has dropped ~4-6% across us-west2 and us-east1. Auto-drains kicked in and there is a small backlog on prod-rt queue. :eyes:
kevin: Any recent rollouts or driver changes? Which pools are affected?
maria: No controlled rollout in the last 24h. Initial signal looks spread across racks rather than single rack. Sample from node logs:```[2026-11-03T06:02:11Z] nvidia: Xid 45 0x7f err; ECC corrected=24 uncorrected=2
[2026-11-03T06:02:12Z] kernel: GPU 3: thermal throttling observed, reset queued
[2026-11-03T06:02:15Z] runtime: prefetch failed for kvcache shard=17, rc=-5```
sam: I see correlated kernel timeouts and prefetch failures in telemetry. Early hypothesis: batch of cards showing intermittent PCIe link flapping causing driver reconnection loops. Not a single driver version standout but skewed toward machines with driver v520.56 and mixed PSU traces.
taylor: @maria can you run `fleetctl ls --filter=zone:us-west2 --status=draining --fields=node,pool,driver` and paste output? Also paging rotation is oncall->eng-infra->eng-runtime.
maria: Pasting minimal output:```node-12 pool-gpu-rtv driver=520.56 status=draining
node-47 pool-gpu-rtv driver=520.56 status=draining
node-98 pool-gpu-batch driver=515.43 status=draining```
devops-bot: [ALERT] autoscaler: us-west2 effective capacity -5.3% vs baseline (1m avg) — scaled down 6 instances to maintain health.
kevin: Are we seeing the same card model? Could be a bad lot from vendor. Anyone have serial-only mapping for the nodes?
sam: Quick mitigation options: 1) pin new allocations to alternate pools that are healthy (us-west2-pool-b and us-east1-pool-c), 2) add a temporary soft-drain policy so we don't hard-reset cards mid-inference, 3) increase prefetch timeout to avoid drop/retry storms. I can push a config for #2 if we agree.
maria: Soft-drain + re-route sounds good. Hard resets are causing Xid churn and make telemetry worse. We'll tag affected nodes with `maintenance:probable-hw-flake`.
taylor: Operational ask: list out expected capacity impact and cost delta if we move traffic to higher-cost pools (estimated +12% token cost this hour due to burst capacity billing). Need approval from infra leads.
kevin: Approve soft-drain and re-route for 2 hours. Sam, please deploy the soft-drain policy. Maria, start a replacement request for nodes with uncorrected ECC > 1 in last 24h and include serials.
maria: Will collect serials and open hw-replace tickets. Also capturing a concise runbook snippet here for oncall:```- mark nodes maintenance:probable-hw-flake
- apply soft-drain policy on affected pools
- route new requests away from pool-gpu-rtv to pool-gpu-b/temp-pool
- monitor Xid/ECC rates for 30m, if uncorrected ECC persists -> escalate to hw-replace
- avoid hard-reset cycles unless explicitly approved by eng-infra leads```
sam: Pushed soft-drain policy to affected pools at 06:06 UTC. Confirming routing change to temp pools.
devops-bot: [INFO] routing: traffic shift completed (06:07:24 UTC) — 88% of prod-rt shifted off pool-gpu-rtv.
maria: After shifting, Xid/s dropped from 14.2 -> 3.1 at 06:15 UTC. Capacity deficit is still ~3% due to replacement in progress but service latency stable. :thumbsup: 
taylor: Good mitigation. Keep monitoring for 2h and collect node serials for vendor RMA. If we see reoccurrence after routing, escalate to oncall-hardware channel.
kevin: Also please add a short postmortem note in incidents once we close—capture cause, mitigation, and cost delta.
maria: Will assemble a short incident summary and serial list. Thanks for rapid responses everyone.
sam: Leaving a watch on metrics for next 3 hours, will ping if anything spikes.
kevin: Great. Closing loop for now. :white_check_mark:
